territory: Newfoundland Power Inc. distributes electricity to most customers on the island of Newfoundland (Public Utilities Act; Electrical Power Control Act, 1994); Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro serves Labrador and the rural districts of the island. Only the postal areas of the towns Newfoundland Power serves whole are taken — the Avalon (A1), Grand Falls-Windsor (A2A, A2B), Corner Brook (A2H), Stephenville (A2N), Clarenville (A5A); the rural postal areas, which the two utilities share, and Labrador are left out
what: electricity for the premises at the organisation's address
period_basis: the distributor's own words on its automatic payments: “Payments are taken directly from your bank account every month.” (https://newfoundlandpower.com/My-Account/Payments/Payment-Options)
delivery: a bill: “At the Bank: Bring your bill to the bank and pay in person.” (https://newfoundlandpower.com/My-Account/Payments/Payment-Options)
payment: through a bank, by automatic payment from a bank account or by cheque; a credit card through a third party, for a fee: “Automatic Payment : Payments are taken directly from your bank account every month.” … “Mail: Send a cheque, money order or MoneyGram to Newfoundland Power at PO Box 8910, St. John’s, NL A1B 3P6 .” … “Credit Card: Pay online using PaySimply . You’ll be charged a small fee.” (https://newfoundlandpower.com/My-Account/Payments/Payment-Options)
terms: “Did you know by paying within 10 business days of your billing date you can receive a 1.5% discount?” (https://newfoundlandpower.com/My-Account/Payments/Payment-Options)

legal_name_basis: as its own rate schedule names it: “Schedule of "Adjusted Rates" Maritime Electric Company, Limited Schedule of Rates Rate Code August 1, 2026” (https://www.maritimeelectric.com/media/q1fcy52a/602000-section-n-28-effective-august-1-2026.pdf, read 2026-11-11)
amount_basis: the service charge of its General Service rate (code 232) in its schedule of rates of August 1, 2026: “232 General Service Service Charge $ 24.57 Demand Charge - per kW for first 20 kW $ - Demand Charge - per kW for balance of kW $ 13.43 Energy Charge per kWh for first 5,000 kWh $ 0.2188” (https://www.maritimeelectric.com/media/q1fcy52a/602000-section-n-28-effective-august-1-2026.pdf); energy by the kilowatt-hour comes on top — this organisation's own consumption is not published
estimate: estimated — about $572 a month before tax for 2,500 kWh a month: calculated from its General Service rate — the service charge of $24.57 + 2,500 kWh × 21.88 ¢: “232 General Service Service Charge $ 24.57 Demand Charge - per kW for first 20 kW $ - Demand Charge - per kW for balance of kW $ 13.43 Energy Charge per kWh for first 5,000 kWh $ 0.2188” (https://www.maritimeelectric.com/media/q1fcy52a/602000-section-n-28-effective-august-1-2026.pdf, read 2026-11-11); 2,500 kWh a month is the use at which the Ontario Energy Board's small-business bill calculator opens (https://www.oeb.ca/_html/calculator/en/electricity/smallbusiness/), taken here as one yardstick for every province; HST is not counted; this organisation's own consumption is not published
